rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization - Maximum Annual Rent Increase
rules.requirement: Landlords may raise rent only once a year, by no more than the lesser of 3% of current rent or 80% of the CPI change. The maximum allowable increase for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027 is 2.87%.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change; 2.87% for 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.extraction_note: Source is a city information page, not the ordinance text. It gives no ordinance number, adoption date, effective date, covered buildings or exemptions. The 2.87% figure applies to the period beginning 2026-09-01, but that is the annual adjustment period, not the ordinance's effective date. Tenants can petition over excess increases. The page also describes a registration-fee pass-through capped at $50 per unit, with overpayments to be reimbursed. That item does not fit any of the six categories and was not extracted separately.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction and Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as nonpayment of rent, lease violation, or owner move-in. For certain eviction reasons, landlords may have to pay relocation assistance toward moving costs.
rules.key_value: Valid cause required (e.g., nonpayment, lease breach, owner move-in); relocation assistance for certain causes
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
rules.extraction_note: The summary is from a city information page and is not the ordinance text. It does not list the full set of causes, notice periods, relocation amounts, coverage, or the ordinance number and dates. On relocation assistance it says only: "If your landlord evicts you for certain reasons, they might have to help pay for your moving costs."
